angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 731,181 km at 131.25 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.6190 +/- 0.0143 mas (same row, RUWE 0.82): 131.25 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.051 +/- 0.013 solar radii from Mantovan et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5398 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A.129M/abstract): 731,181 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.146 +/- 0.013 solar masses from Mantovan et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5398 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A.129M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6000 +/- 75 K from Mantovan et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5398 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A.129M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mantovan et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5398 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A.129M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5398.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.454, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
